reasons: The redline is a true insertion: the only change to p0072 is the added proviso barring Kubient from assigning to a Customer competitor without our consent; all Customer-favourable mechanics (affiliate/successor carve-out, 'not unreasonably withheld' consent standard, binding-on-successors language) are preserved, so the failed changed-character ratio check is an artefact and not a substantive over-edit.

Directionally correct and actionable: it closes the only identified gap (Vendor's unconsented ability to assign to a competitor via the mutual carve-out) without giving up the existing mutual bargain, consistent with the rule's fallback plus the preferred 'never to a Customer competitor' element.

Rationale is verified against the cited text: the clause already grants Customer affiliate/M&A assignment rights and there is no change-of-control termination, re-pricing, or 'deemed an assignment' trigger, so no walk-away condition exists and no further deletion is required.
Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and in first person plural; it states what changed, why, and confirms Customer's own assignment rights are untouched.
Residual risk after the edit is narrow (Vendor assignment to a competitor now needs our consent), so the high severity overstates the remaining exposure; medium is more apt.
